title: Bile & Emulsification
page_title: Bile & Emulsification | Cambridge (CIE) IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences (Double Award) Revision Notes 2023

blocks.md: - Cells in the liver produce bile which is then stored in the **gall bladder**

blocks.alt: Bile production and secretion, IGCSE & GCSE Biology revision notes

blocks.md:
- It is **alkaline** to **neutralise the hydrochloric acid** entering the duodenum from the stomach
- The enzymes in the small intestine have a higher (more alkaline) optimum pH than those in the stomach
- It **breaks down large drops of fat into smaller ones**. This is known as **emulsification**. The larger surface area allows lipase to chemically break down the lipid into glycerol and fatty acids faster

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: Emulsification is the equivalent of tearing a large piece of paper into smaller pieces of paper. This is an example of **mechanical digestion**, not chemical digestion – breaking something into smaller pieces does not break bonds or change the chemical structure of the molecules which make it up, which is the definition of chemical digestion.
